personas.name: Sam
personas.tag: One synced passkey — the floor, honestly stated
personas.bio: Sam wants zero homework: one synced passkey, done. Setup shows the wizard adapting to a one-item inventory; recovery shows that passkey surviving a lost laptop.

steps.story: Sam opens the wallet and gets the nudge: no recovery path yet. The honesty note is right there — recovery helps if you lose your key, it cannot stop someone who already has it.
steps.spec: Flow B · decision 2 (nudge each open) · decision 6 (honest copy)

steps.story: The tab lands on three preset shapes — you pick ONE. Sam wants his hand held instead: “Guide me”.
steps.spec: Flow C · decisions 3/75 — presets landing (pick one shape) + Guide me / Customize

steps.story: One screen of education, three bullets, no jargon. The key fact: his address never changes.
The inventory: Sam ticks only “Another device” — and the single-method note appears: one method is allowed, but whatever removes it locks you out.
steps.spec: Step 2 · the note renders only for one-item inventories · new state screen

steps.story: One method, one path: “Passkey alone”. The lockout note is permanent here — whatever removes that method locks you out. 48 hours stays at the default — he never needs the waiting-period step.
steps.spec: Step 3 · decision 37 philosophy at the floor · new screen from the persona round

steps.story: No passkey exists yet. The wizard asks the device to create one. (The drawn side rail lists the generic three-method inventory.)
The operating system takes over: Touch ID does the biometrics. The wallet never sees them.
Created and detected: “Synced passkey — iCloud Keychain”. The access test is still required — nothing saves before it passes.
Test passed. The synced detection matters: usable from any signed-in device — remember that line, it is Sam's whole recovery story.
Before the save: the rehearsal. Sam completes his one row as if the key were lost today — locally, nothing on-chain.
steps.spec: Decision 47 — the dry run · new screen

steps.story: One path, one method, 48 hours, one signature. Nothing touched the chain until now. (Bridge: the drawn review includes the hidden-details panel; Sam skipped the recovery password.)
steps.spec: Step 8 of 10 · atomic save · 48h default stands for single-method paths (decision 74)

steps.story: One transaction, confirmed. His path is live from this moment.
The Recovery Card holds the address and instructions — nothing else. He turns alerts on: they are his cancel-window tripwire.
steps.spec: Step 9 of 10 · card contents decided · decision 11

steps.story: Months later: the laptop is gone. On the new machine, a fresh install offers the third door.
steps.spec: Flow A — recovery is a first-class entry point

steps.story: The anti-scam gate: no support agent will ever ask you to do this.
Extension password for the new machine. The fast-track is short on purpose.
A new key, backed up. It will receive the account; the address never changes.
He reads his address off the Recovery Card. Looking it up is harmless and starts nothing.
Identity confirmed before anything is collected. The summary shows THE path: Passkey · 48h.
steps.spec: Confirming starts nothing · one path per account (decision 73) · single-method variant

steps.story: The whole checklist is one row. This device has no passkey — but his phone does, because the passkey is synced. He scans the QR; the phone signs.
steps.spec: Decision 17 (platform sync + hybrid QR) · new screen · same verify-in-place panel as D-07b

steps.story: The consent screen: the account, the new key, 48 hours. The owner can cancel — that is the protection. (Bridge: the drawn summary reads the generic passkey + guardians shape; his is the single passkey.)
steps.spec: Flow D chapter 3 · funding/executor still open (Q7/Q19)

steps.story: The countdown runs on-chain. He closes the browser; nobody cancels. (Same generic summary as the consent screen.)

His again. The old laptop is still signed in to iCloud, so the synced passkey stays reachable from it — flagged. Order matters: add a new passkey on this machine first, then remove the flagged one — never drop your only method.

personas.name: Alice
personas.tag: Five paper guardians, zero platform dependence
personas.bio: Alice keeps keys on paper and hardware, air-gapped. Setup: the People-only preset, five addresses, 72 hours. Recovery: three approvals, one signed on a machine that never goes online.

steps.story: Alice gets the same nudge as everyone. Her answer will look nothing like Sam's.
She picks the only preset with no passkey: “Guardians only”. Picking it makes it her single recovery path — she skips the inventory and lands at enrollment.
Five guardians, entered as addresses and one ENS. No names anywhere — the wallet stores nothing that could reveal who her people are. A paper key in a safe counts.
steps.spec: Decision 43 (a guardian is an address) · decision 39 · new screen

steps.story: She sets the waiting period to 72 hours — one waiting period for the whole path. Her paper keys live in a safe out of town; she wants time, not speed.
She hides the values: five addresses behind a password. Anyone can still read her path's shape — not who her people are. Set once; forgetting it never locks her out.
steps.spec: Decisions 48/56 · what exactly gets hidden is open (53)

steps.story: The rehearsal: her guardian rows cannot sign without asking her people, so they rehearse as reachability checks. (Bridge: the rehearsal’s drawn addresses differ from her enrolled five.)
steps.spec: Decision 47 · decision 52 — guardian rows rehearse as reachability only

steps.story: The review is her exact shape: one path, one lone group, any 3 of these 5 members, 72 hours.
steps.spec: Decision 41 — a lone ANY-of group is the whole path · new screen

steps.story: One transaction, confirmed. Her lone-group path is live.
She prints the card and files it with her paper keys. It deliberately omits her guardians — the configuration is the secret, the address is not.
steps.spec: Card exclusion list · guardian addresses stay off the card

steps.story: Her laptop dies. New machine, fresh install, third door.
The anti-scam gate. Nobody asked her to do this.
Extension password for the new install.
A new key; the words go on paper — her preferred material.
The address comes off her Recovery Card.
Right account — and the summary is hers exactly: one path, any 3 of 5 members, 72h.
Her one path, confirmed — not chosen: there is nothing to choose. Five people, any 3 of them; the addresses stay hidden (Q29) — she knows who her people are.

The checklist IS the group — no passkey row exists. She sends each guardian the link, the same way she talks to them anyway. Two answers are already in — and one guardian declined, so she asks another of her five.
steps.spec: Decision 35 · new screen — no required rows

steps.story: A guardian's phone. Plain language first, and one required pause: contact the owner on a channel you already had.
steps.spec: Flow E1 · decision 9 — ignorable but verifiable

steps.story: This guardian's key never touches the internet. The page has a path for exactly that.
Copy the message, sign it on the air-gapped machine, carry the signature back, paste it.
steps.spec: E1-04b — the air-gapped ceremony, step by step

steps.story: Signed. Nothing was sent anywhere — the guardian sends it back to Alice themselves.
steps.spec: E1 default: approvals travel person to person

steps.story: Back on Alice's machine: she pastes the approval. Two done, one to go — the others land the same way, in any order.
steps.spec: Paste-time validation · approvals have no expiry

steps.story: The third approval lands the same way: 3 of 3 — the group is satisfied and Continue unlocks.
Consent: the account, the new key, and — for her — 72 hours. (Bridge: the drawn rows read 48h and a passkey path.)
Three days of waiting is her choice working as designed. (Bridge: the drawn countdown reads 48h and a passkey path — hers is 72h, guardians only.)
Hers again — and nothing to clean up: no method was tied to the dead laptop. Her five people stay exactly as they were.

personas.name: Carl
personas.tag: Synced passkey + Sara — both sides of one favor
personas.bio: Carl is not technical. His path: his passkey AND his friend Sara's wallet. He loses his laptop; his phone still holds the synced passkey — and Sara does the rest. This journey walks both sides.

steps.story: The first preset is Carl’s family — your device + your guardians. He picks it; the wizard trims the group to Sara alone.
Enrollment starts immediately. The OS draws the Touch ID sheet. (The drawn side rail lists the generic three-method inventory.)
“Synced passkey — iCloud Keychain.” That one detected line is the seed of his whole recovery.
One guardian row: Sara's wallet, entered as an address. The wallet checks the checksum and the ENS — and stores no name.
steps.spec: Decision 43 · the screen is drawn with exactly one guardian

steps.story: Carl hides Sara's address behind a password. The Recovery Card in the drawer stays a non-map.
The rehearsal: his passkey signs for real; Sara's row rehearses as reachable.
The review is his exact shape: passkey AND any 1 of 1 member — Sara's address — 48 hours.
steps.spec: Decision 36 — 1-of-1 groups are legal · new screen

steps.story: One transaction, confirmed. His path is live.
The card goes in a drawer. It will matter.
Carl's laptop is gone. On a borrowed machine: fresh install, third door.
No support agent will ever ask you to do this. Nobody did.
A quick password for this install.
The new key that will receive the account.
The address comes off his Recovery Card.
Right account, before anything is collected. (Bridge: the drawn summary shows the generic 2-of-3 group; his group is Sara alone.)

No choosing — this IS his path: the passkey AND Sara, both required, and both reachable today: the passkey is synced, Sara is a phone call away. (Bridge: the drawn readout shows a 2-of-3 group; his is Sara required.)
steps.spec: Decision 73 — one path · decision 29 — values may be hidden

steps.story: “This device has no passkey for the account — use the phone that has it.” His phone is safe and signed in; he scans the QR and the phone signs. (The drawn group card is mid-recovery — one approval already shows.)
steps.spec: Decision 17 — platform sync + hybrid QR · verify-in-place (decision 35)

steps.story: The passkey row flips to Complete. (Bridge: the drawn row reads “signed on this device”; in his story the phone signed over the QR hand-off.)
steps.spec: Decision 35 — the passkey step, now visibly done

steps.story: Sara's phone. She calls Carl first — the sign button stays locked until she confirms she did.
Signed — and nothing sent anywhere. Sara copies the approval and sends it back on the same channel as the call.

Sara’s first approval does not take: she opened an old link, so it was made for a different recovery request. The paste is rejected on the spot, with the reason. She opens the fresh link, signs again — the new approval lands. (Bridge: the drawn group reads 2 of 3; his needs only Sara.)
“Both rows complete” — literally his path: one required row, one group. 48 hours start now. (Bridge: the drawn summary reads the generic 2-of-3 shape.)
He closes the borrowed browser. The state persists. (Same generic summary.)
His again. One flag: the synced passkey — the lost laptop stays signed in to the platform account, so it can still use it. Add a fresh passkey on this machine first, then revoke the old one.

personas.name: Diana
personas.bio: Diana has a passkey and a long-lived email, and nobody she’d ask to be a guardian. The wizard gives her one group: any 1 of 2 — either alone recovers. When her device dies and her platform account is unreachable, the email is her way back.

steps.story: Diana wants protection with no other people involved. Guided route.
She ticks “Another device” and “A long-lived email”. Nothing else — and that is fine.
The wizard does NOT recommend passkey AND email — at her level, locking herself out is the bigger risk. One group instead: any 1 of 2, either alone recovers. This screen is her config verbatim.
The device creates her passkey; the OS sheet does the ceremony. (The drawn side rail lists the generic three-method inventory.)
Detected as synced (iCloud Keychain) — remember that for later. Test passed.

The email check, on the real mechanic: she clicks “Send email”, the message arrives at her enrolled address, she downloads the original .eml and uploads it — the wallet checks it locally. (Subject format and prover still open — Q16.)
One waiting period covers the whole path — she keeps 48 hours.
Her email address gets hidden too. She needs this password only to read her own setup during a recovery — forgetting it never blocks the recovery itself.
steps.spec: Decisions 48/56 · D-06e is the wrong-password state

steps.story: The rehearsal covers the group: either row alone completes it; the email row runs the same send-and-upload check in miniature. Drawn mid-rehearsal.
The review is her config verbatim: one path — any 1 of 2: passkey, email. 48 hours.
One transaction saves the path — confirmed and live.
Recovery Card into a drawer; alerts on.
Her device is gone, and her platform account is unreachable from the new machine — the phone that could confirm the sign-in was the lost device. Fresh install.
steps.spec: The synced-passkey trap: the platform account is the real root

steps.story: The gate. Nobody asked her to do this.
Password for the new install.
New key, twelve words on paper.
Address from the Recovery Card.
The chain answers with her path: any 1 of 2 — passkey or email. The email is her way back. (Bridge: the drawn summary is the generic passkey + guardians shape; hers is any 1 of 2 — passkey or email.)

The passkey row says “Not available on this device” — marked, never disabled: the wallet cannot know it is truly gone. The group needs any 1 of 2, so the email alone still recovers. Values stay hidden (Q29) — she knows her own inbox.

One row: “Send email”, the message arrives, she uploads the original .eml, and the wallet creates the proof on this device (~60s). Row complete. (Bridge: the drawn checklist shows the generic shape mid-recovery; her run is the single email row.)
steps.spec: Decision 77 · decision 35 — the verify panel IS the checklist for a one-row path

steps.story: Consent: the account, the new key, 48 hours. (Bridge: her path row reads Email · 1 row complete.)
The countdown is also her safety: if this were an attacker, she could cancel. (Bridge: the drawn summary reads the generic shape.)
Recovered. The dead passkey is flagged — this screen fits her exactly: remove “MacBook passkey”, keep the email, add a passkey on the new machine. (Bridge: the guardians row is not hers.)
steps.spec: Decision 20 · D-15 drawn almost for Diana

personas.name: Bob
personas.tag: 2-of-3 across distinct roots — recovery, then an attack
personas.bio: Bob is technical: one lone group, any 2 of 3 — passkey, email, hardware-wallet guardian. Three acts: he builds it, he uses it without the lost passkey, and when the lost laptop's holder strikes back, the design holds.

steps.story: Bob skips the hand-holding.
steps.spec: Flow C · Advanced is an action, not a mode

steps.story: The builder: ONE path canvas — nothing required, one group. His config to the letter: any 2 of 3 — passkey, email, a guardian. The last member is going in now.
steps.spec: Decisions 41/73/75 · the filter-builder pattern users already know

steps.story: The picker: anything already in the path is greyed out — one instance, one slot. His hardware wallet isn’t enrolled yet: “Enroll something new”, and he pastes its address.
steps.spec: Decisions 43/76 — by address, no names · instance uniqueness

steps.story: Group complete, 48h on the path — the picker starts at the 24-hour floor. Advanced has its own terminal: save as one transaction, no wizard review. The optional password row lives in the right rail — the same component as the wizard step.
steps.spec: Decision 74 — 24h contract floor · the advanced flow never routes through the wizard

steps.story: Even the advanced path gets the rehearsal: any 2 of 3, satisfied locally. (Drawn in wizard chrome — the advanced entry is a bridge.)
Saved as one transaction — confirmed. The builder shows the result read-only.
The result: the overview shows THE path — structure, threshold, 48h — with Edit and Remove. Members live inside path editing.
Months later his main laptop is stolen — but a second machine is logged in. Recovery starts from Settings: the condensed warning, then which account receives control.
steps.spec: Flow D additions · decision 34 · 40 — only Bob can demo the logged-in entry

steps.story: The lost account's address, from memory — he is Bob.
Confirmed — and the summary is his: one path, any 2 of 3 members (passkey · person · email), 48h.
His path is read back: any 2 of 3. The passkey member sits on the stolen laptop — the email and his guardian will answer. The values stay hidden (Q29).
steps.spec: Decision 41 · new screen · Q29 values hidden

steps.story: Member one, the email: “Send email”, the original .eml uploaded, proof generated on-device. Complete. (Bridge: the drawn checklist shows the generic required-passkey shape; his run is the lone group — email first.)
Member two: the hardware-wallet guardian — himself, on the guardian page. Same rules: verify, confirm contact, sign.
steps.spec: Flow E1 — the page treats every guardian alike

steps.story: Signed on the hardware wallet; the approval travels back by hand.
Email done — 1 of 2 for the group. The passkey row reads “Not reachable from this device”: marked, never disabled. The guardian approval will close the group.
steps.spec: Decision 41 · new screen — an unreachable member is never removed, just not used

steps.story: 2 of 2 — the group is satisfied without the passkey. The unreachable member stays listed, unused.
Consent, 48 hours. (Bridge: his row reads “any 2 of these 3 members — 2 of 2”.) (The drawn row also claims the passkey answered — in his story it did not.)
The countdown runs. (Bridge: the drawn summary reads the generic passkey shape.)

Recovered. The stolen laptop's passkey is flagged — and Bob, in a hurry, defers the cleanup. Watch what that costs. (Bridge: the drawn cleanup list is the generic fixture; his real flag is the laptop passkey.)
steps.spec: Decision 20 · the deferral is allowed — and tracked

steps.story: The overview will not let him forget: “Until you replace it, the account can be recovered again by whoever holds that device.” That sentence is about to come true.
steps.spec: Decision 46 — deferral is a state, not a screen

steps.story: Days later: somebody started recovering his account. The thief has the flagged passkey AND the laptop's logged-in inbox — two of three members. Banner + notification; Bob knows it wasn't him.
steps.spec: Flow D2 · decision 11 · a 2-of-3 attack needs two members — both lived on the stolen laptop

steps.story: Cancel is not resolution — the thief still holds working methods. The required triage shows what the request had satisfied. (Bridge: for Bob that was the passkey and the email.)
steps.spec: Flow D2 — triage is required, not optional

steps.story: Replace means edit the path: swap the stolen members out, right in the editor. (Bridge: the drawn path shape differs.)
steps.spec: Decision 45 — methods are managed inside path editing

steps.story: One signed transaction later: clean overview, no flag. The design held.
steps.spec: End of the attack — and of the demo

personas.name: Rollout
personas.tag: MVP · V1 · V2 — what ships when
personas.bio: Not a journey: the milestone split (decision 79) laid over the same flows — what the MVP must carry, what V1 adds, and what waits for V2, with the risk the MVP accepts stated plainly.

steps.story: The rollout in one picture. MVP = one person can protect one account and recover it, with all four methods and preset shapes only. V1 adds the guided layer and the hosted guardian page. V2 adds scale and upkeep — cleanup, triage, multi-account, health checks. The bottom strip names what the MVP knowingly leaves open.
steps.spec: Decision 79 · team exhibit — maps to no persona journey

personas.name: Extras
personas.bio: Not part of any persona story: the provisional wizard states (drawn dashed — they will probably be removed) and the all-methods dry-run master for development.

steps.story: PROVISIONAL — the optional guardian test-sign: ask a guardian to sign a test message, paste the reply back; saving is never blocked. Drawn dashed; the dry run may replace it.
PROVISIONAL — the mid-wizard access recheck strip. The decision-47 dry run covers the same need in-session; drawn for the meeting's request.
The all-methods dry-run master: passkey, guardians, email and Aadhaar in one rehearsal, plus the password-recall row. A development reference — no persona has all four methods.
steps.spec: Decision 47 · the recall row is the forget-protection (56)

steps.story: The help sheet behind “How do I get the .eml?”: per-client steps for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, Yahoo and Proton. Opened from both the setup check (C-05e) and the recovery row (D-07e).
steps.spec: Decision 77 — per-client steps to be verified by the kit team

steps.story: Three policy grammars side by side: the old OR-of-paths, today’s required-AND-groups model (decision 73), and the lone ANY-of group — which is today’s model with nothing required. Built to share with the team; it maps to no persona journey.
